brief.topic: The Light Shared Between Nine Small Squares

s01: Step away from a small lantern and its light spreads into more space.
The lantern has not become weaker.
The same outgoing light is being shared.
Imagine a tiny source in clear space, with no nearby reflections.
Follow one small bundle of its light.
Twice as far away, the bundle is twice as wide and twice as tall.
That makes four times the area.
The same energy now passes through four equal patches instead of one.
Each patch receives one quarter as much light per second.
This is the inverse square relationship.
Distance is squared because the spreading happens across an area.
A real lantern has a shape, and walls can send light back.
The tiny-source model works best when distance is large compared with the lamp.
The shaded squares represent energy, not how brightness must look to your eyes.
Move the screen to three times the original distance.
The bundle now covers nine of the original patches.
Each receives one ninth as much.
Bring the screen close again, and the same light gathers into the smaller patch.

scenes.narration:
Step away from a small lantern and its light spreads into more space. The lantern has not become weaker. The same outgoing light is being shared.

Imagine a tiny source in clear space, with no nearby reflections. Follow one small bundle of its light. Twice as far away, the bundle is twice as wide and twice as tall. That makes four times the area.

The same energy now passes through four equal patches instead of one. Each patch receives one quarter as much light per second. This is the inverse square relationship. Distance is squared because the spreading happens across an area.

A real lantern has a shape, and walls can send light back. The tiny-source model works best when distance is large compared with the lamp. The shaded squares represent energy, not how brightness must look to your eyes.

Move the screen to three times the original distance. The bundle now covers nine of the original patches. Each receives one ninth as much. Bring the screen close again, and the same light gathers into the smaller patch.
